title: A chart whose colour tokens do not resolve paints black and says nothing
foundBy: a consumer migrating to the published build, who met it on every graph view they have

evidence.verified:
`npm run ci` exits 0 with 86 test files where there were 85, the visual gate at 112 of 112 and 0 differing pixels, and size:subpaths passing.

Measured on the artifact rather than the source, which is the failure mode a development-only guard invites and which this project has been caught by before. The built `dist/lib/chartTheme.js` was rendered through `renderToString` in a jsdom document: with no tokens defined it emits both warnings, with the tokens defined it emits none, and with `NODE_ENV=production` it emits none. That is the published file warning, not the source.

Each mechanism was proved load-bearing by mutation rather than assumed. Removing the two calls fails 3 of the 5 tests; dropping the guard that a single defined token means the sheet is there fails 2; dropping the once-per-family dedup fails 1. The file was restored and git diff read clean.

The tests take a fresh module per case, and re-import the renderer beside it so one React stays in the graph. A warning that fires once per family for the life of the module would otherwise let a later test assert on silence it had not earned.

details:
`readVars` in `src/lib/chartTheme.ts` reads every colour with `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue(name).trim()`. A custom property that is not defined is not an error: `getPropertyValue` answers with an empty string. So `theme.graph` becomes an array of empty strings, a mark drawn with `fill=""` is invalid, and the browser paints it black.

Nothing anywhere says so. The package installs, the types are satisfied, the build succeeds and the page renders. A consumer reported exactly this: they installed a dev build published before `--color-graph-*` existed, and every categorical colour in every graph view came out black, with a clean typecheck and no console output.

The tokens can be absent for reasons that have nothing to do with a stale build. A consumer who imports `styles/components.css` but not `styles/core.css` has no tokens at all. One who scopes the token sheet to a subtree and renders a chart outside it has none either. All three land in the same place, and none of them is told.

This kit already treats this class of failure as worth a warning. `warnWhenUnstyled` exists because a component rendering with no stylesheet looks like a component that rendered, and one application shipped that way unnoticed. An empty palette is the same failure one layer down.

notes.text:
The instrument already exists and the guard is the one this file uses elsewhere. `warnPastSlots` in the same module warns when `assignSeriesColors` is asked for more series than a ramp keeps apart, once per case, behind `process.env.NODE_ENV` rather than `import.meta.env.DEV`, so it survives into a consumer's development build. A warning for an empty palette copies that shape.

Where it goes matters. `readVars` already branches on whether there is a document: the no-document branch returns empty strings deliberately, because that is server rendering and empty is correct there. The check belongs in the other branch, where a document exists and an empty token therefore means the stylesheet is missing rather than the environment is.

Whoever writes it should confirm it survives into `dist/` by running the built file, not the source. A development-only guard that compiles to nothing is how this project has been caught before, and every test still passed.

One judgement in the predicate worth stating. It warns only when every slot in a family is empty, not when one is. A single defined token means the stylesheet is present, so a gap in the middle is a different fault and a different conversation; treating it as this one would warn on a consumer who deliberately overrides part of a ramp. There is a test for that case.
